overrides.reason: Strict-pre-vote SF1750 section 13 creates mandatory association participation in unit-owner dispute resolution before debt collection, with no user fee; other sections limit fines, foreclosure/attorney fees and establish conflict-of-interest controls. These are concrete purchaser/owner protections and oversight changes in the exact HOA/CIC sector identified in Bahner's source statement.

The exact pre-vote HF3684 version directs Veterans Affairs to apply measurable grant scoring and authorizes withholding grants for grantee fraud or criminal investigation; it also requires recipients to report program use and results. Those are substantive controls for public grant money that match Robbins's broadly stated state-program fraud oversight and accountability position.

HF4252 section 10 creates §136A.1212, allowing denial of state student aid or grants for materially false/fraudulent applications, refusal of reasonable state information or inspection requests, or established government-funding fraud. This is a concrete fraud-control mechanism for a state program, directly within Robbins's public-money accountability proposition.

The strict pre-vote SF4760 article 18 adds BCA subpoena authority for financial crimes and fraud expressly including investigations of state-funded or administered programs or services. A new investigatory tool for state-program fraud is substantively aligned with Robbins's support for stronger state oversight and accountability; no private-fraud or unrelated policy identity is transferred.

HF3900's frozen March 18 first engrossment would submit a permanent school fund constitutional amendment to voters and implement a 4.5-percent trailing asset-value distribution formula. The proposed ballot question explicitly aims to increase funding going to all Minnesota school districts without increased individual income/property taxes. It aligns with Hussein's source-specific support for strong, well-resourced public schools statewide; the proposal is contingent on voter adoption, not treated as already enacted.

HF3732 sections 2-5 materially broaden support services for at-risk youth education/training and section 10 establishes a Pathways to Prosperity program for adult basic education, GEDs and occupation credentials. These are real workforce/education pathways, but most are DEED employment services and carry forward existing youth programs, not a clear K-12/student education-system reform that expands career pathways as required by Kresha's combined source proposition. Without proving the precise education-reform element, remain fail-closed.

SF4760 article 18 newly requires Department of Commerce referrals to BCA of crimes uncovered by its civil insurance-fraud investigations and separately authorizes BCA subpoenas for financial/public-program fraud. Although this creates a reporting obligation for one state agency and a separate enforcement tool, the reporting relates to commercial insurance crimes while the tool spans public-program investigations; the exact source proposition joins stricter state-agency fraud reporting with tools to identify/prevent fraudulent activities. The mismatched program scope cannot be safely inferred to satisfy the combined proposition, so no direction or applicability is assigned.
